title: Noun sentence - Identifying components
description: Identify the 3 components of a noun sentence (جُمْلَة اسْمِيَّة) — Mubtada, Khabar, and Muta'allaq bil khabar — in 7 Quranic ayat with their surah and ayah number, including special mudhaafs that build the Muta'allaq bil khabar.
source: Owner's lesson notes on the noun sentence (Mubtada, Khabar, Muta'allaq bil khabar, special mudhaafs), with Quranic examples (Ash-Shura 42:19, Al-Baqarah 2:20/39/95/153, Al-Fatihah 1:2, Al-Asr 103:2)

questions.text: What are the 3 components of a noun sentence?

options.text: Mubtada, Khabar, and Muta'allaq bil khabar
Harf of Nasb, Jaar Majroor, and Khabar
Mubtada, Khabar, and Harf of Nasb
Mubtada, Jaar Majroor, and special mudhaaf

questions.explanation: The three components of a noun sentence are Mubtada (M), Khabar (K), and Muta'allaq bil khabar (MBK).

questions.text: In the formula M(must) + is + K (optional) + MBK (optional), which component is the only one that is required?

options.text: Khabar
Mubtada
Muta'allaq bil khabar
Both Khabar and Muta'allaq bil khabar

questions.explanation: The formula marks Mubtada as "must", while Khabar and Muta'allaq bil khabar are both optional.

questions.text: When a sentence begins with a harf of Nasb, what is the Mubtada?

options.text: The first Raf'a in the sentence, regardless of the harf of Nasb
The Khabar that follows the harf of Nasb
The harf of Nasb and its ism, including chain
The harf of Nasb alone, without its ism

questions.explanation: The Mubtada is a harf of Nasb and its ism including chain, when a harf of Nasb is present.

questions.text: When there is no harf of Nasb in the sentence, what is the Mubtada?

options.text: The Khabar
The Muta'allaq bil khabar
Whatever word comes first in the sentence, status aside
The first Raf'a in the sentence, including chain

questions.explanation: Without a harf of Nasb, the Mubtada is simply the first Raf'a in the sentence, including its chain.

questions.text: How is the Khabar defined?

options.text: The first Raf'a after the Mubtada, including chain
A Jaar Majroor that follows the Mubtada
The ism of the harf of Nasb
Any Raf'a anywhere in the sentence

questions.explanation: The Khabar is the first Raf'a that comes after the Mubtada (including its chain), and it gives information about the Mubtada.

questions.text: What can function as the Muta'allaq bil khabar (MBK)?

options.text: Only a second Khabar
A Jaar Majroor including chain, or a special mudhaaf and its mudhaaf ilaih, including chain
Only the harf of Nasb's ism
Only a Raf'a word

questions.explanation: The Muta'allaq bil khabar is additional information given as a Jaar Majroor (including chain) or a special mudhaaf and its mudhaaf ilaih (including chain).

questions.text: In "اللَّهُ لَطِيفٌ بِعِبَادِهِ" (Ash-Shura 42:19, "Allah is Subtle with His servants"), what is the Mubtada?

options.text: لَطِيفٌ
بِعِبَادِهِ
اللَّهُ
عِبَادِهِ alone

questions.explanation: There is no harf of Nasb in this ayah, so the Mubtada is the first Raf'a, اللَّهُ.

questions.text: In the same ayah, "اللَّهُ لَطِيفٌ بِعِبَادِهِ", which word is the Khabar, and which part is the Muta'allaq bil khabar?

options.text: Khabar: بِعِبَادِهِ; Muta'allaq bil khabar: لَطِيفٌ
Khabar: اللَّهُ; Muta'allaq bil khabar: لَطِيفٌ
There is no Khabar, only a Muta'allaq bil khabar
Khabar: لَطِيفٌ; Muta'allaq bil khabar: بِعِبَادِهِ

questions.explanation: لَطِيفٌ is the first Raf'a after the Mubtada, so it is the Khabar; بِعِبَادِهِ (a Jaar Majroor) is extra information, the Muta'allaq bil khabar.

questions.text: In "إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ" (Al-Baqarah 2:20, "Indeed, Allah is able to do all things"), what is the Mubtada?

options.text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ
اللَّهَ alone, without إِنَّ
عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ
قَدِيرٌ

questions.explanation: The Mubtada is the harf of Nasb together with its ism, including chain — so إِنَّ اللَّهَ (the whole chain) is the Mubtada, not اللَّهَ by itself.

questions.text: In the same ayah, "إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ", where does the Khabar come, and what is the Muta'allaq bil khabar built from?

options.text: Khabar: عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ; Muta'allaq bil khabar: قَدِيرٌ
Khabar: قَدِيرٌ (the first Raf'a after the Mubtada); Muta'allaq bil khabar: عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ, where كُلِّ is one of the special mudhaafs
Khabar: كُلِّ شَيْءٍ; Muta'allaq bil khabar: قَدِيرٌ
There is no Khabar in this ayah

questions.explanation: Even though عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ comes first in the sentence, قَدِيرٌ is still the first Raf'a after the Mubtada, so it is the Khabar. عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ is the Muta'allaq bil khabar, a Jaar Majroor whose chain includes the special mudhaaf كُلِّ.

questions.text: In "وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ" (Al-Baqarah 2:95, "And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers"), what is the Mubtada?

options.text: عَلِيمٌ
بِالظَّالِمِينَ
اللَّهُ
الظَّالِمِينَ alone

questions.explanation: There is no harf of Nasb in this ayah, so the Mubtada is the first Raf'a, اللَّهُ.

questions.text: In the same ayah, "وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ", which word is the Khabar, and which is the Muta'allaq bil khabar?

options.text: Both عَلِيمٌ and بِالظَّالِمِينَ are Khabar
Khabar: بِالظَّالِمِينَ; Muta'allaq bil khabar: عَلِيمٌ
Khabar: اللَّهُ; Muta'allaq bil khabar: عَلِيمٌ
Khabar: عَلِيمٌ; Muta'allaq bil khabar: بِالظَّالِمِينَ

questions.explanation: عَلِيمٌ is the first Raf'a after the Mubtada, so it is the Khabar; بِالظَّالِمِينَ (a Jaar Majroor) is the Muta'allaq bil khabar.

questions.text: In "هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ" (Al-Baqarah 2:39, "They will abide therein forever"), what is the Mubtada?

options.text: هُمْ
فِيهَا
خَالِدُونَ
There is no Mubtada

questions.explanation: هُمْ is an independent pronoun and is not joined to فِيهَا by any fragment, so it is the first Raf'a and the Mubtada.

questions.text: In the same ayah, "هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ", which word is the Khabar, and which is the Muta'allaq bil khabar?

options.text: Khabar: هُمْ; Muta'allaq bil khabar: خَالِدُونَ
Khabar: خَالِدُونَ; Muta'allaq bil khabar: فِيهَا
Khabar: فِيهَا; Muta'allaq bil khabar: خَالِدُونَ
There is no Khabar, only a Muta'allaq bil khabar

questions.explanation: خَالِدُونَ is the first Raf'a after the Mubtada, so it is the Khabar, even though فِيهَا (the Muta'allaq bil khabar, a Jaar Majroor) comes before it in the sentence.

questions.text: In "الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ" (Al-Fatihah 1:2, "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds"), what is the Mubtada?

options.text: لِلَّهِ
رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
الْحَمْدُ
الْعَالَمِينَ alone

questions.explanation: There is no harf of Nasb in this ayah, so the Mubtada is the first Raf'a, الْحَمْدُ.

questions.text: In the same ayah, "الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ", what role does لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ play?

options.text: It is the Mubtada
It is still the Khabar
It is a harf of Nasb
It is the Muta'allaq bil khabar, a Jaar Majroor standing in for the missing Khabar

questions.explanation: With no Khabar stated, لِلَّهِ (a Jaar Majroor, with رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ continuing its chain) functions as the Muta'allaq bil khabar.

questions.text: In "إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ" (Al-Asr 103:2, "Indeed, mankind is in loss"), what is the Mubtada?

options.text: إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ
الْإِنسَانَ alone, without إِنَّ
إِنَّ alone
لَفِي خُسْرٍ

questions.explanation: The Mubtada is the harf of Nasb together with its ism, including chain — so إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ (the whole chain) is the Mubtada, not الْإِنسَانَ or إِنَّ by itself.

questions.text: In the same ayah, "إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ", what role does لَفِي خُسْرٍ play?

options.text: It is the Khabar
It is the Muta'allaq bil khabar, a Jaar Majroor standing in for the missing Khabar
It is a second ism of إِنَّ
It is the Mubtada

questions.explanation: The لَ here is only emphasis; فِي خُسْرٍ is a Jaar Majroor, and with no Khabar stated, it functions as the Muta'allaq bil khabar.

questions.text: In "إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ" (Al-Baqarah 2:153, "Indeed, Allah is with the patient"), what is the Mubtada?

options.text: اللَّهَ alone, without إِنَّ
مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ
إِنَّ اللَّهَ
إِنَّ alone

questions.explanation: The Mubtada is the harf of Nasb together with its ism, including chain — so إِنَّ اللَّهَ (the whole chain) is the Mubtada, not اللَّهَ or إِنَّ by itself.

questions.text: In the same ayah, "إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ", what role does مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ play, and what kind of word is مَعَ?

options.text: It is the Khabar, and مَعَ is a harf of Nasb
It is the Mubtada, and مَعَ is a Jaar Majroor
It is a second ism of إِنَّ, and مَعَ is a pointing word
It is the Muta'allaq bil khabar standing in for the missing Khabar, and مَعَ is one of the special mudhaafs

questions.explanation: With no Khabar stated, مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ functions as the Muta'allaq bil khabar. مَعَ is one of the special mudhaafs — it always appears as a mudhaaf (here to الصَّابِرِينَ) without meaning possession.
